1500.author: yuanzhou75
1500.body:
## What this fixes

The rail paints `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png` at 32x32 on a `#f5f5f5` surface. Since `6614a0c4` ("switch logo, app mark and Windows icon to the rounded light variant") that PNG fills its whole 128x128 canvas with a white rounded square - 93.6% of its pixels are fully opaque and 60.3% are pure white - so the rail shows a white tile with the mark inside it instead of the mark itself.

This replaces the asset with the transparent cut of the official light artwork, corrects the stylesheet comment that described a tile, and gives the shell's first-run pages the same cut so one launch does not change the mark halfway through. Three files: the PNG, `design.css` (comment), `application/scripts/build.mjs` (the copy source).

## How the asset was made

- Source: the official vertical light logo, rendered at 8x on a transparent page.
- The wordmark is everything below the fully transparent band at y=471-564 of that render; the mark above it is 320x372 px there.
- Crop: a square canvas sized on the mark's long side (394 px at 8x, ~6% above and below), resized to 128x128 with Lanczos, RGBA.
- Measured on the file that ships, with explicit thresholds: ink box (`alpha > 0`) 109x126 px inside 128, margins 10 px left, 9 px right, 1 px above and below; `alpha = 255` on 29.6% of the canvas, `alpha = 0` on 55.1%, and the remaining 15.3% partial. At `background-size: 32px` that draws the mark at about 27x31.5 px - it is a tall mark, so it fills the box vertically and keeps its air on the sides.
- The file keeps the 128 px size the stylesheet asks for, so `background-size: 32px 32px` and `border-radius: 8px` are untouched.

## Where the mark is painted

Six surfaces paint it, all on a light background:

| surface | rule / file | background |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rail | `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css:90` | `#f5f5f5` (`.rail`) |
| sign-in page header | `apps/desktop/src/styles/login.css:36` | `#fff` (`.login-page`) |
| setup-wizard header | `apps/desktop/src/styles/wizard.css:59` | `#fff` (`.wizard-page`) |
| 技能 › 从 GitHub 导入 | `apps/desktop/src/styles/settings.css:1807` | `#fff` (settings dialog) |
| shell loading page | `application/src/loading.html` (`.wizard-brand-mark`) | `#fff` |
| shell first-run page | `application/src/wizard.html` (same rule) | `#fff` |

The last two load `app-mark.png` from `dist/`, which `application/scripts/build.mjs` writes - now from the renderer's asset, so they paint this file too.

The remaining three mentions do not paint anything themselves: `apps/desktop/src/views/Rail.tsx:76` and `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/SkillGitImportView.tsx:259` name it in a comment and a class name, and `application/scripts/build.mjs` is the copy step.

## The shell pages paint the same cut

Before this branch `build.mjs` copied `application/build/icon-256.png` to `dist/app-mark.png`, so the pages that load before React painted the old tile at 24x26 px inside the 32 px box while the rail painted 28x30 px - the mark changed as the loading page handed over to the SPA.

The fix is not to make `icon-256.png` transparent. That one file has three jobs:

- `dist/icon.png` - the tray image (`application/src/main.ts:1601`), which sits on unknown desktop backgrounds and needs its tile;
- the OLD source of `dist/app-mark.png`, the shell brand row, until this branch;
- the 256 frame `application/scripts/make-icon.ps1` wraps into `build/icon.ico` for the installer and taskbar.

So `build.mjs` now copies the renderer's transparent asset to `dist/app-mark.png` and leaves `dist/icon.png` exactly where it was: the UI gets the transparent cut, the system icons keep the opaque one.

Verified by running those two copy statements as written (same `join`/`cpSync` expressions) in the shell package: `dist/app-mark.png` comes out byte-identical to `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png` (md5 `9263f9c9...`) and `dist/icon.png` byte-identical to `build/icon-256.png` (md5 `5081a365...`), so the tray image did not move. `node --check application/scripts/build.mjs` exits 0. The whole script could not be run here - the shell package's `node_modules` are not installed in this checkout and esbuild stops on `electron-updater` - so the esbuild half was not executed; the copy half is what this diff changes, and that is what I ran.

## Frames

Pinned to commit `97142e04` on `yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery:screenshots-appmark`, not to a branch name. Harness: `apps/desktop/e2e` - Vite on its own port, `fixtures.ts` answers every `/api/**` request; viewport 1280x820, DPR 1, zh-CN. The only difference between a "before" and its "after" is `app-mark.png`.

![rail mark, before and after, 2x](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-after-rail-2x.png)

| frame | what it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [before-rail-160.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-rail-160.png) | the rail's top-left corner as shipped: white rounded tile, 32 px |
| [after-rail-160.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/after-rail-160.png) | the same corner with this head: the mark on `#f5f5f5`, no tile |
| [before-window-1280.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-window-1280.png) | the whole 1280x820 window before |
| [after-window-1280.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/after-window-1280.png) | the whole 1280x820 window after |
| [before-login-brand.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-login-brand.png) | the sign-in header at 32 px on `#fff`, before |
| [after-login-brand.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/after-login-brand.png) | the same header after: on white the tile was invisible already, so only the mark itself differs |

**Two of the six surfaces have no frame here.** The setup-wizard header and the skill-import marks were not captured: the wizard needs an account session (the fixtures answer `/api/**` but not the account service, so the app falls back to the sign-in page), and the skill-import dialog did not open from the skills pane under these mocks. Nothing in this description is a capture of either. Their rules are the same shape as the sign-in header - 32 px, same asset, `#fff` - which is why the sign-in pair stands in for them, not because they were photographed. The two shell pages are not captured either: they are plain HTML outside the renderer and need the packaged shell to boot.

`raw.githubusercontent.com` did not answer from this machine while I was writing this, so each file was checked through the contents API at that commit instead: every remote size equals the local byte count exactly.

## Not changed on purpose

- `docs/images/logo.png` and the installer icons (`application/build/icon-256.png`, `icon.ico`, `icon.icns`) keep their tile: an OS icon is shown against unknown desktop backgrounds, and a transparent one would disappear on a dark taskbar. Switching those to the new artwork is a separate change, not this one.
- `border-radius: 8px` on `.rail-logo` stays: it has no visible effect on a transparent asset and keeps the rule correct if a filled asset is ever used again.

## Testing

- No runtime logic changed: one binary asset, one CSS comment, and one copy source in `application/scripts/build.mjs`. It does change what two shell pages paint - they now draw the same cut at the same size as the rail, where they drew 24x26 px before.
- No unit test asserts the pixels of the mark and I did not add one - a jsdom test cannot read the PNG's alpha without a decoder dependency, and the frames above are what a person can actually check.
- `L1`, `UT` and `ST` do not read this asset, and the CSS edit is inside a comment; the shell copy is exercised by the `application` build in the packaging job, not by those suites.
1500.head: fix/transparent-app-mark
1500.title: fix(desktop): draw the rail mark without the white tile

1501.author: qingkwl
1501.body:
## Problem

osx-sign's `isbinaryfile` probe misjudges ~2500 pure DATA files as Mach-O (NUL bytes in the first 8000) and walks them into the per-file `codesign --timestamp` loop. Two signed builds (2026-11-25, m5 tree) both died mid-marathon with:

```
A timestamp was expected but was not found
```

The ~2h / ~2500-roundtrip timestamp load trips Apple's TSA rate limit, killing the whole `SD_MAC_SIGN=1` release build.

## Change

Extend `mac.signIgnore` (electron-builder.yml) with 13 patterns covering the misjudged cohorts. Cohorts were verified by scanning the actual release bundle (92376 files):

| Cohort | Pattern(s) | ~Files |
|---|---|---|
| timezone blobs | `zoneinfo/` | 598 + ~500 (tzdata/pytz) |
| PDF CMap tables | `/cmap/` | ~212 + 148 (`*.json.gz`) |
| numpy/scipy/sklearn test data | `/tests?/data/`, `/datasets/(data|images)/`, `.npz`, `.mat`, `.sav`, `.wav`, `.fits` | ~560 |
| fonts / static libs / misc | `reportlab/fonts/`, `.a`, `.pfb`, `/babel/locale-data/`, `/mpl-data/` | ~60 |

## Why this is safe

- Skipped files stay in the bundle and remain covered by the **CodeResources seal hashes** — notarization and Gatekeeper are unaffected (same treatment as the existing `.pyc` entry, same story as `.kext` upstream).
- Pattern set validated over the whole bundle: **2555 files matched, 0 true Mach-O harmed** (`.so` 259 / `.dylib` 23 / `bin/python` 2 all still signed).

## Verification

End-to-end proof on this tree (main @ `9e91f78b` + this patch), `SD_MAC_SIGN=1 bash scripts/build-mac.sh`:

- codesign verify OK (Developer ID + hardened runtime, identity match)
- signing completed in ~40 min, **no TSA throttling** (previously died at ~2h)
- `.app` notarized + staple validated; DMG notarized (Submission `91305035-b615-468f-8f15-7eed4ab19e2f`, Accepted) + staple validated
- `spctl -a -vv` accepted for both DMG and `.app` (source=Notarized Developer ID)

Ad-hoc smoke builds (the default, no `SD_MAC_SIGN`) are unaffected — `signIgnore` only feeds the signing path.
1501.head: fix/w23a-signignore-data-files
1501.title: fix(mac-signing): exempt pure data files from per-file codesign timestamping (W23a)

1504.author: yuanzhou75
1504.body:
Closes #1502.

Hint text across the settings panel, the session flyout and the document tabs was drawn below WCAG AA: `.settings-field-hint` at 3.95:1 on the panel, `.settings-ability-option-hint` at 3.95:1 on white and 3.71:1 on the selected option's `#f4f8ff`, `.session-flyout-desc` at 3.36:1 and 3.08:1 on a hovered row, `.session-flyout-note` and `.expert-note` at 3.36:1, `.doc-tab-hint` — the folder that tells two same-named documents apart — at 2.43:1, and the two field counters plus the capability divider at 2.43:1. All of it is 11–12.5 px normal-weight text, so WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 applies at 4.5:1; none of it is an icon, a placeholder or a disabled control.

## What changed

- `tokens.css` gains `--text-hint: #666666`, the value already agreed for the desktop's sidebar hints in #1486 — one secondary colour for hints rather than a fourth shade. `--muted`, `--muted-light` and `--text-faint` keep their values and their call sites: roughly 250 of them, several not text at all, so lifting those would repaint the shell to fix these rules.
- **Nine** rules now name `var(--text-hint)` and nothing else — no per-surface override, no literal left behind: `.settings-field-hint`, `.settings-ability-option-hint`, `.settings-field-count`, `.settings-textarea-count`, `.settings-ability-divider`, `.session-flyout-desc`, `.session-flyout-note`, `.expert-note`, `.doc-tab-hint`.

## One correction to the report, with the evidence

`.doc-tab-hint` is measured in #1502 at **2.14:1** on `--surface-sunk #f0f0f0`, described as "the workspace panel". The panel a reader sees is white: three sheets name `.workspace-panel` — `workspace.css:18` paints it `var(--surface-sunk)`, `workspace.css:169` paints it `var(--surface)`, and `design.css:2495` paints it `#fff` — and `index.css` imports `design.css` **after** `workspace.css`, so the winning declaration is the white one. The folder line is therefore **2.43:1**, not 2.14:1: far below the floor either way, so the defect stands, but the record should carry the number a reader actually meets.

The darker surface is still held **defensively**: the test measures the rule on `--surface-sunk` as well, so the value keeps clearing AA if those later declarations ever go away.

## The frames

All four pairs are real runs of the desktop harness (mocked control plane, no service), rendered at 2× so an 11–12.5 px line is legible. The settings frame is the 专家 form's capability block, which holds both settings hints: the one under the field and the one inside the default-selected full-access option.

| surface | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| capability block: field hint 12.5 px, option hint 12 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-settings.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-settings.png) |
| field counters `0 / 80`, `0 / 500`, 12 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-counters.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-counters.png) |
| flyout description, 12 px, row hovered | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-flyout.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-flyout.png) |
| document tab folder line, 11 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-doctab.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-doctab.png) |

Each frame was taken in the same run as a `getComputedStyle` read of the element it shows:

| hint | before | after | surface behind it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.settings-field-hint` | `rgb(128, 128, 128)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |
| `.settings-ability-option-hint` | `rgb(128, 128, 128)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(244, 248, 255)` = `--primary-softer` |
| `.settings-field-count` | `rgb(166, 166, 166)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |
| `.session-flyout-desc` | `rgb(140, 140, 140)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |
| `.doc-tab-hint` | `rgb(166, 166, 166)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |

## Verification

`apps/desktop/tests/hint-contrast-surfaces.test.ts` — seven cases. It reads the sheets, resolves `--text-hint` through `tokens.css`, and asserts 4.5:1 for **each surface a rule is actually painted on**:

```
.settings-field-hint #666666 on settings #ffffff        = 5.74:1
.settings-ability-option-hint #666666 on settings        = 5.74:1
.settings-ability-option-hint #666666 on selectedOption  = 5.39:1
.settings-field-count #666666 on settings                = 5.74:1
.settings-textarea-count #666666 on settings             = 5.74:1
.settings-ability-divider #666666 on settings            = 5.74:1
.session-flyout-desc #666666 on flyout #ffffff           = 5.74:1
.session-flyout-desc #666666 on flyoutHover #f5f5f5      = 5.27:1
.session-flyout-note #666666 on flyout #ffffff           = 5.74:1
.expert-note        #666666 on flyout #ffffff            = 5.74:1
.doc-tab-hint       #666666 on panel #ffffff             = 5.74:1
.doc-tab-hint       #666666 on sunk #f0f0f0              = 5.04:1
```

Beyond the ratios it asserts: each rule declares exactly one colour and names the token; no other rule repaints a hint (only the documented `.settings-field-hint.is-error`, which stays `--danger`); the surfaces it measures are the ones the sheets paint (including the `index.css` load order that decides the panel colour); and the shared muted tokens keep their values.

The pairing itself is asserted, not assumed: the hint inside `.settings-ability-option` is `.settings-ability-option-hint`, so one case reads `SpecialistForm.tsx`, takes the capability option's `<label>…</label>` slice and requires the option's own hint to be inside it, `.settings-field-hint` **not** to be, and the label to carry `is-selected`. That is the mistake this suite had before: it measured `.settings-field-hint` against `#f4f8ff`, a surface that rule never touches.

Mutation runs, each making the test red:

- `.settings-ability-option-hint` back to `#808080` → **3 failed**;
- the option rendering its hint with the `settings-field-hint` class instead (the old wrong pairing, in the DOM) → **1 failed**: `the hint paired with the selected option is the one rendered inside it`;
- `.doc-tab-hint` back to `#a6a6a6` → **3 failed**;
- `--text-hint: #767676`, a grey that clears white at 4.54:1 and nothing else → **2 failed** (`.settings-ability-option-hint #767676 on selectedOption #f4f8ff is 4.26:1`);
- a hover override `#6a6a6a` on a correct base — "each surface passes" with two colours → **1 failed** (repainted hint).

`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` is clean. `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs` — 234 passed. The desktop unit suite reports 55 failing cases on this WSL host **both with and without the change** — the same files in both runs (the comparison is a `git stash` of this diff) — so they are pre-existing here, not this diff; the new test is green in both runs.

## Scope notes

- `.settings-ability-divider` ("或指定") is not in the report's table. It is the same colour and size, in the same block, on the same surface, and it read 2.43:1, so it moved with the rest; say the word if dividers should stay decorative instead.
- Rules with a hint colour that this report does not name are untouched — e.g. `.expert-desc` (`#8c8c8c`, 3.36:1 on white) in the 专家 flyout. They are the same defect on other rows and belong in a follow-up rather than silently widening this one.

## Merge order with #1491

**#1504 lands first.** This pull request is in the merge queue (`QUEUED`, enqueued 2026-11-27 11:05:29Z); #1491 has no merge-queue entry and is still `REVIEW_REQUIRED` (head `9b1881ae`).

Landing first breaks nothing: this branch carries its own `--text-hint: #666666` declaration, so it is complete on its own. The cost moves to #1491, which rebases onto this one after it lands and resolves the `tokens.css` comment hunk from the other side. Both insert the declaration at the same anchor — right after `--text-faint: #8c8c8c;` — each with its own comment, so **that rebase is a conflict to resolve by hand, not an auto-merge**: the resolved hunk keeps one declaration and one comment that covers both halves (the sidebar and landing surfaces #1491 is about, and the settings and flyout surfaces here). The token name and value are identical on purpose, so no shade diverges; the only thing that can go wrong is two declarations of the same name surviving, where the last would win silently.

## The owner's look

The owner has looked at all four pairs on this head:

- **2026-11-27 18:43 CST** — the settings, flyout and document-tab pairs: he answered the question card 「#1502 这三处提示文字的改动，你看过帧了吗？」 with 「认可，去求票」. Recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/1504#issuecomment-7216242552).
- **2026-11-27 19:22 CST** — the counters pair added afterwards: he answered 「补的这对计数行帧（`0 / 80`、`0 / 500`）认可吗？」 with 「认可，一起去求票」. Recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/1504#issuecomment-7216992841).

A different head or a new set of frames needs another look from him.
1504.head: fix-1502-hint-contrast
1504.title: fix(desktop): raise settings, flyout and document-tab hint text to WCAG AA

1505.author: yuanzhou75
1505.body:
Comment- and metadata-only follow-up to #1496 (merged in `6b4b574a`). This is the one follow-up both reviews asked for and deferred rather than blocking on: `zhaozhaozz` noted the rationale above `.drop-overlay` "still says a drop is about the session behind a dialog, not about the dialog, which this change reverses, so only that sentence needs a pass", and the review that followed recorded the other two as non-blocking with "land them as the single follow-up you described after this merges".

No behaviour changes: no code path, no selector, and no product string is touched.

**What changed** (3 files, +20/−13)

1. `apps/desktop/src/styles/overlays.css` — the comment above `.drop-overlay` now describes what the layer does after #1496: a drag belongs to the surface under the pointer, and over a dialog that surface is the dialog (no overlay is raised there), so the layer's remaining job is to stay under the two scrims for the moment a dialog opens mid-drag. It keeps the existing statement that it has to cover the three columns. The z-index pair named in the comment is the measured one: `.config-backdrop` 1200, `.modal-backdrop` 1300, `.drop-overlay` 500.
2. `apps/desktop/src/app/use-file-drop.ts` — the `useFileDrop` JSDoc had ended up above the `DIALOG_SURFACE` constant. It is back on the exported function it documents; its wording is unchanged, and `DIALOG_SURFACE` and `insideDialog` keep their own one-line comments.
3. `apps/desktop/e2e/session-import-drop.spec.ts` — the spec's `E2E-META` `Steps:` named only the first of its five cases. It now covers all five, in the multi-line numbered form `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs` accepts.

1507.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
1507.body:
Mocked daily/release batches run the nine JiuwenSwarm checks once, on the owning batch's stack. A retried case inherited `checks: 'run'`, so the retry repeated the checks on a second stack and wrote `e2e/jiuwenswarm-checks.json` into `<batch>-retry`; merge-gate's `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` then correctly reported UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS for a passing retry.

## What changed
- `test/support/tagged/retry-runner.mjs`: `batchLaunchConfig()` accepts `retry` and emits `checks: 'off'` for every retry slice; `isolatedRetryConfig()` sets it. First attempts keep their `run`/`off`/undefined behaviour, so the one-shot checks evidence is unchanged.
- `.ci/mocked-report.mjs` is untouched: no `*-retry` whitelist. A retry directory passes only because it holds no checks file; a checks file there or in any other non-designated `mocked-*` directory still fails with UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS.
- Tests: a checks-carrying-batch regression and an audit guard (files below).

## Validation
- `node --test test/support/tagged/tests/retry-environment.test.mjs`: 4 pass / 1 fail before the fix (`actual: 'run', expected: 'off'`), 5 pass / 0 fail after.
- `node --test .ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs`: 11 pass / 0 fail; whitelisting `*-retry` makes the guard fail.
- `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`: 243 pass / 0 fail.
- `node --test test/support/tagged/tests/*.test.mjs`: 75 pass / 6 fail / 1 skipped; the 6 `PYTHON_COLLECTION_FAILED` cases need python3 pytest and fail identically on the baseline.
- `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`: BLOCKED (`BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`: no bwrap, user namespaces denied), 0 executed.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED: the mocked browser layer needs the JiuwenSwarm stack, Chromium and the bubblewrap sandbox, none available here. The tests cover the retry configuration and the report's strictness; CI's mocked E2E job is the first true end-to-end run.

## Release
Release category: release:internal
User impact: none; CI retry tooling only.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #1506

```
node --test test/support/tagged/tests/retry-environment.test.mjs && node --test .ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs
```
